recipes.name: Cucumber Tomato Salad with Sweet Lime Vinaigrette
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon white sugar, or to taste
2 medium tomatoes, seeded and cut into wedges

steps.text: Make the dressing: Stir vinegar, lime juice, and sugar together in a small bowl until sugar dissolves.

Make the salad: Hold cucumber upright and use a peeler to remove strips of peel lengthwise, making a pattern of peeled and unpeeled strips all the way around for a decorative effect. Cut cucumber in half lengthwise, then thinly slice each half.
Place cucumber into a salad bowl with tomatoes and red onion; mix to combine. Pour dressing over salad and mix until well combined. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Just before serving, stir cilantro into salad and sprinkle chopped peanuts over top.

raw_recipe.headline: Cucumber Tomato Salad with Sweet Lime Vinaigrette
raw_recipe.description: This delicious cucumber and tomato salad is tossed with fresh cilantro and crushed peanuts in a sweet and tangy dressing of rice vinegar, lime juice, and sugar.

review.reviewBody: We had a super spicy red curry tonight - and this salad was a great cool-down! I added a little more sugar, otherwise made as written. Thanks for the recipe! :)

I am a thai food lover so this salad looked like the perfect way to use up the 2 cups of cherry tomatoes I was gifted with by a neighbor. I made this with those cherry tomatoes and diced the cucumber. I substituted raw turbinado sugar for the white + 1 tsp agave nectar to keep the glycemic load as low as possible yet achieve the desired amount of sweetness; I used vidalia onion instead of red. I used 1 tsp coriander seed because I had no fresh cilantro. I used prepared lime juice. I used equal parts seasoned and plain rice vinegars. I did add chopped peanuts for authentic thai taste. I marinated everything in a flat glass pyrex storage dish and turned it upside down at intervals so everything could marinate equally. This is a very mild flavor, the thai-style dressing allows the taste of the veggies to shine through. I could eat this with every meal because it's so colorful, light and healthy. If you appreciate thai food, you will like this. My picky 13 year old enjoys it as much as I do. A complement to burgers, chicken, fish, stir fry, practically everything. I will make this again and again with the changes I listed above. Would be great for office potlucks or picnics.

Awesome! I made this for the first time and took it to a potluck and everyone raved about it. I had huge cucumbers and tomatoes from the garden so seeded and chopped them all for less liquid. Used a sweet onion instead of red. Because I had so many veggies I had to triple the dressing but did add just one extra teaspoon of sugar and a splash of sesame oil. I obviously used way more cilantro because of the amount of salad I made and I mixed it in with the dressing so I wouldn't have to do it at the party. Kept the peanuts on the side so people could choose to have them or not. I was a little nervous to try a new recipe on my husbands family but it was a hit! Thank you for a great way to use up those garden cukes!

This really turned out well. The only changes I made was to dice the veggies into similar size chunks, salt them and let them sit a few minutes to drain a little. I also added a couple of shakes of garlic powder as everything could use a bit of garlic (grin). Thanks for a wonderful recipe!
Try adding a sweet fruit like mango or pineapple. I substituted organic raw honey for the sugar, and added chickpeas to make it more hearty.
Very good for the faint of heart. I add 1/4 cup fish sauce-1/4 cup white vinegar-1/4 cup cold good water. Then thinly slice one jalapeno or three thai bird peppers. YUM

I think I know the "something missing" ingredients some reviewers mentioned. This needs a teeny bit of peanut oil and some fresh chopped thai basil. It will make all the difference, trust me. If you have never had thai basil it has a lovely anise taste and aroma but very subtle. This recipe could also use some very thinly sliced radish to add the heat some felt it needed. With those modifications, it will be fabulous.

I followed the recipe exactly. I did not add peanuts since I'm not a huge fan. There's a very mild flavor but it's extremely fresh tasting. I'd make this again for sure. Maybe next time I will use halved cherry tomatoes and chop the cukes into cubes.
This is a really nice cucumber salad variation. I don't care for cilantro, so I substituted parsley. I also used yellow tomatoes and red tomatoes to give it even more color. It was a big hit.
Had this tonight along side of baked salmon. Very good, easy to put together and didn't change a thing except for using sugar substitute instead of white sugar in the dressing. Keeper!!
Great starter recipe. I added chopped snow peas, sweet peppers, parsley. Also added Shirachri (?) rooster sauce to the dressing. Gave it a nice kick.
Great as is
Thai Cucumber Tomato Salad by Sherriel. Even better with a little crushed red pepper. Second favorite.
This is a keeper. I made it exactly as directed. Next time I may add some red pepper for some kick. Super refreshing.
Made it as directed. A nice change for a salad.
I changed the cilantro to fresh basil from the garden. Just made sense to me.
